rotation_note: Unattended-run override: NO rotating subset. All 3 core keywords plus the entire politics pool (34 keywords, grouped into policy_regulation / elections_public_opinion / geopolitics) are working keywords today. Day-of-year 309 sets ORDER only: group start index 309 % 3 = 0 (elections_public_opinion leads, then geopolitics, then policy_regulation), and within each group the list starts at offset 309 % group_size in pool order (elections 9 -> 3: AI disinformation first; geopolitics 10 -> 9: 소버린 AI first; policy 15 -> 9: AI procurement rules first). Queries were not checked with WebSearch (budget reserved for librarians); librarians should prefer outlet RSS/sitemap_news feeds over site: search for recency. Window: last brief was 2026-11-04, so items published 11-04 (after the prior harvest) through 11-05 are in scope. Context: two days after the US midterm Election Day. In scope: official post-election statements/after-action reports on AI-enabled interference (CISA/FBI/ODNI, state election officials), platform post-election takedown/labeling reports, certified results of AI-specific ballot measures (data center siting/moratoria, AI-related propositions), FEC/FCC actions, and lame-duck agenda items only when a bill is introduced/marked up or an official release names AI. OUT of scope: who won, seat counts, polling, horse-race analysis, and 'did AI money win' commentary. EU: the Commission's 2027 work programme leak was covered 11-04 — the officially adopted text is the SAME story unless it adds an AI item not in the leak; informal European Council in Dublin on AI 2026-11-13 is upcoming (official pre-meeting papers are new; previews are not). Neutrality rule from sources.json applies: report decisions/filings/releases, attribute contested claims, no partisan framing.
